## What is wrong (one paragraph)
Since #1037 (KS-1101) the gateway's `/health/deep` reports a soft-down dependency as `degraded` instead of `up`. `scripts/smoke-test.sh` reads that aggregator in section 1 and its branch at `:107` treats ANYTHING that is not `up` as a failure, so a degraded service reds the whole smoke test (the gate measured 5 pass / 0 fail becoming 4 pass / 1 fail). Kam ruled (2026-09-22 18:11, option a): **`degraded` is a PASS WITH A WARNING that names the service; `down` / `error` (anything else) still fail.** The change is ONE `elif` arm between the `up` branch and the `else` branch: it calls the script's existing `pass` helper (so the service counts in `PASS`) and its existing `warn` helper (so `WARN` counts it and the `!` line names the service and its status). Nothing else in the script changes: the `up` arm, the `else`/`fail` arm, the python parser, the counters and the RESULTS block are untouched. NOT in this task: `/health/deep` itself, the api-gateway, any other section of the smoke test.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh - a 'degraded' /health/deep
# service passes WITH a warning that names it; 'down'/'error' still fail
# (KS-1245, Kam's ruling 2026-09-22 option a)
# =============================================================================
# curl is NEVER run here (no stack, no network): it is a STUB on a private
# PATH, in the shape of container_trivy_failed_scan_is_loud.test.sh. The stub
# answers /health/deep with the fixture's JSON and every http_code probe with
# 200, so under --quick only section 1 of the smoke test can fail.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/smoke_test_degraded_warns.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
SMOKE="$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh"
[ -f "$SMOKE" ] || { echo "FATAL: smoke-test.sh not found at $SMOKE" >&2; exit 2; }

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1245.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# A /health/deep body with the five services at the given statuses.
deep_body() {
  printf '{"ready":true,"status":"x","checks":{"redis":{"status":"%s","latencyMs":1},"postgres":{"status":"%s","latencyMs":2},"auth":{"status":"%s","latencyMs":3},"originate":{"status":"%s","latencyMs":4},"anchoring":{"status":"%s","latencyMs":5}}}' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5"
}

# Build a fixture: $1 = dir, $2 = the /health/deep body the stub curl returns.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" deep="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/bin"
  printf '%s' "$deep" > "$root/deep.json"
  sed "s#@ROOT@#$root#g" > "$root/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in */health/deep) cat "@ROOT@/deep.json"; exit 0 ;; esac
done
for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = "-w" ] && { printf '200'; exit 0; }; done
exit 0
STUB
  chmod +x "$root/bin/curl"
}

# Run the smoke test in --quick mode with the stub curl first on PATH. Prints rc.
run_smoke() {
  local root="$1"
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; bash "$SMOKE" --quick ) > "$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
count() { grep -c -F "$2" "$1/out.txt"; }

# CONTROL - every service 'up': rc 0, no failure, no warning.
build_fixture "$WORK/allup" "$(deep_body up up up up up)"
got="$(run_smoke "$WORK/allup") $(count "$WORK/allup" 'Failed: 0') $(count "$WORK/allup" 'Warnings: 0')"
if [ "$got" = "0 1 1" ]; then ok "CONTROL - five services up: rc 0, Failed: 0, Warnings: 0"; else bad "CONTROL - five services up: rc 0, Failed: 0, Warnings: 0" "want 0 1 1, got $got"; fi

# RED - auth 'degraded', the rest up: the run passes (rc 0) with ONE warning that names auth and its status.
build_fixture "$WORK/degraded" "$(deep_body up up degraded up up)"
got="$(run_smoke "$WORK/degraded") $(count "$WORK/degraded" 'Warnings: 1') $(count "$WORK/degraded" 'auth - status=degraded')"
if [ "$got" = "0 1 1" ]; then ok "RED a degraded service passes the smoke test with one warning naming the service and its status"; else bad "RED a degraded service passes the smoke test with one warning naming the service and its status" "want 0 1 1, got $got"; fi
got="$(count "$WORK/degraded" 'Passed: 13') $(count "$WORK/degraded" 'Failed: 0')"
if [ "$got" = "1 1" ]; then ok "RED the degraded service is COUNTED as passed (Passed: 13, Failed: 0), not as a failure"; else bad "RED the degraded service is COUNTED as passed (Passed: 13, Failed: 0), not as a failure" "want 1 1, got $got"; fi

# CONTROL - postgres 'down': still a failure (rc 1) naming the service and status, on both trees.
build_fixture "$WORK/down" "$(deep_body up down up up up)"
got="$(run_smoke "$WORK/down") $(count "$WORK/down" 'Failed: 1') $(count "$WORK/down" 'status=down')"
if [ "$got" = "1 1 2" ]; then ok "CONTROL - a down service still fails the smoke test (rc 1, Failed: 1, postgres named twice: the line and the FAILURES list)"; else bad "CONTROL - a down service still fails the smoke test (rc 1, Failed: 1, postgres named twice: the line and the FAILURES list)" "want 1 1 2, got $got"; fi

# CONTROL - anchoring 'error': still a failure, on both trees.
build_fixture "$WORK/error" "$(deep_body up up up up error)"
got="$(run_smoke "$WORK/error") $(count "$WORK/error" 'Failed: 1') $(count "$WORK/error" 'status=error')"
if [ "$got" = "1 1 2" ]; then ok "CONTROL - an error service still fails the smoke test (rc 1, Failed: 1)"; else bad "CONTROL - an error service still fails the smoke test (rc 1, Failed: 1)" "want 1 1 2, got $got"; fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# SECUURA PLATFORM — SMOKE TEST
# =============================================================================
# Verifies all services, APIs, and frontend portals are operational.
# Run after: container restart, code deploy, or any infrastructure change.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/smoke-test.sh           # Full test
#   ./scripts/smoke-test.sh --quick   # Health checks only (no API tests)
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m'

PASS=0
FAIL=0
WARN=0
FAILURES=()

pass() { ((PASS++)); printf "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
fail() { ((FAIL++)); FAILURES+=("$1"); printf "  ${RED}✗${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
warn() { ((WARN++)); printf "  ${YELLOW}!${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
section() { printf "\n${CYAN}━━━ %s ━━━${NC}\n" "$1"; }

check_health() {
  local name="$1" url="$2"
  local resp
  resp=$(curl -s -m 5 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || { fail "$name — unreachable"; return; }
  if echo "$resp" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status') in ('healthy','ok') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "$name"
  else
    fail "$name — unhealthy response"
  fi
}

check_http() {
  local name="$1" url="$2" expected="${3:-200}"
  local code
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || { fail "$name — connection refused"; return; }
  if [ "$code" = "$expected" ]; then
    pass "$name (HTTP $code)"
  else
    fail "$name — expected HTTP $expected, got $code"
  fi
}

check_api() {
  local name="$1" method="$2" url="$3" data="${4:-}" expected="${5:-}" auth="${6:-}"
  local resp code auth_header=""
  [ -n "$auth" ] && auth_header="-H \"Authorization: Bearer $auth\""
  if [ "$method" = "POST" ] && [ -n "$data" ]; then
    if [ -n "$auth" ]; then
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $auth" -d "$data" 2>/dev/null)
    else
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$data" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
  else
    if [ -n "$auth" ]; then
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 "$url" -H "Authorization: Bearer $auth" 2>/dev/null)
    else
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 "$url" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
  fi
  code=$(echo "$resp" | tail -1)
  body=$(echo "$resp" | sed '$d')

  if [ -n "$expected" ]; then
    if echo "$body" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if $expected else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
      pass "$name"
    else
      fail "$name — assertion failed"
    fi
  elif [ "$code" = "200" ] || [ "$code" = "201" ]; then
    pass "$name (HTTP $code)"
  else
    fail "$name (HTTP $code)"
  fi
}

# =========================================================================
section "1. BACKEND SERVICE HEALTH (via gateway aggregator)"
# =========================================================================
# F-03 (audit 2026-05-15): rewritten from per-port direct checks to the
# gateway's /health/deep aggregator. The legacy form
# (`http://localhost:6003/health` etc.) tested an older architecture where
# every service was host-port-exposed; in the current docker-compose only
# the nginx gateway, postgres and redis are exposed. The previous form
# returned 22/29 false-failures on a healthy stack.
#
# `/health/deep` is exposed by nginx-gateway → api-gateway, returns
# JSON like {ready, status, checks: {redis, postgres, auth, originate,
# anchoring}}. Each service entry has {status: 'up'|'down', latencyMs}.
DEEP_RESP=$(curl -s -m 10 "$GATEWAY/health/deep" 2>/dev/null) || DEEP_RESP=""
if [ -z "$DEEP_RESP" ]; then
  fail "Gateway /health/deep — unreachable"
else
  # Use python3 (already a hard dep elsewhere in this script) to parse.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r svc status latency; do
    [ -z "$svc" ] && continue
    if [ "$status" = "up" ]; then
      pass "$svc (latency ${latency}ms)"
    else
      fail "$svc — status=$status"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s' "$DEEP_RESP" | python3 -c "
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    for name, info in (d.get('checks') or {}).items():
        status = info.get('status', '?')
        latency = info.get('latencyMs', '?')
        print(name + '\t' + str(status) + '\t' + str(latency))
except Exception as e:
    sys.stderr.write('parse-error: ' + str(e) + '\n')
")
fi

# =========================================================================
section "2. FRONTEND PORTALS"
# =========================================================================
check_http "Issuer Portal" "$GATEWAY/"
check_http "Verifier Portal" "$GATEWAY/verify/"
check_http "Admin Portal" "$GATEWAY/admin/"
check_http "Status Page" "$GATEWAY/status/"
check_http "Website" "$GATEWAY/website/"
check_http "Showcase" "$GATEWAY/showcase/"

# =========================================================================
section "3. API GATEWAY"
# =========================================================================
check_http "Gateway health" "$GATEWAY/health"
check_http "API root" "$GATEWAY/api/"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--quick" ]; then
  section "QUICK MODE — skipping API tests"
else
  # =========================================================================
  section "4. AUTH API"
  # =========================================================================
  check_api "Login (demo)" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    '{"email":"demo@secuura.io","password":"demo123"}' \
    "d.get('success') and d.get('data',{}).get('accessToken')"

  check_api "Password reject (short)" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/register" \
    '{"email":"smoke@t.io","password":"abc"}' \
    "not d.get('success')"

  check_api "Forgot password" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/forgot-password" \
    '{"email":"demo@secuura.io"}' \
    "d.get('success')"

  # Get auth token for protected endpoints
  TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email":"demo@secuura.io","password":"demo123"}' | \
    python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['accessToken'])" 2>/dev/null) || TOKEN=""

  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    pass "Auth token obtained"
  else
    fail "Auth token — could not obtain"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "5. DOCUMENT API"
  # =========================================================================
  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    check_api "List documents" "GET" "$GATEWAY/api/documents" "" \
      "len(d.get('documents',[])) > 0" "$TOKEN"

    # Create a test document with unique hash each run
    SMOKE_HASH=$(python3 -c "import hashlib,time;print('sha256:'+hashlib.sha256(str(time.time()).encode()).hexdigest())" 2>/dev/null)
    DOC_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/documents" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -d "{\"title\":\"Smoke-Test\",\"type\":\"certificate\",\"contentHash\":\"$SMOKE_HASH\"}" 2>/dev/null)
    DOC_ID=$(echo "$DOC_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('id',''))" 2>/dev/null) || DOC_ID=""

    if [ -n "$DOC_ID" ]; then
      pass "Create document ($DOC_ID)"
    else
      fail "Create document"
    fi

    # Verify document gets anchored (auto-anchor fires on creation in dev mode)
    if [ -n "$DOC_ID" ]; then
      sleep 2  # allow async auto-anchor to complete
      DOC_STATUS=$(curl -s "$GATEWAY/api/documents/$DOC_ID" \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
      if echo "$DOC_STATUS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status')=='anchored' or d.get('error','')=='Document is already anchored' else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
        SIMULATED=$(echo "$DOC_STATUS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('blockchain',{}).get('simulated',False))" 2>/dev/null)
        pass "Anchor document (auto-anchored, simulated=$SIMULATED)"
      else
        # Try explicit anchor as fallback
        ANCHOR_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/documents/$DOC_ID/anchor" \
          -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
        if echo "$ANCHOR_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status')=='anchored' or 'already anchored' in d.get('error','') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
          pass "Anchor document (explicit anchor)"
        else
          fail "Anchor document"
        fi
      fi
    fi

    # Verify document
    check_api "Verify document" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/verification/verify" \
      "{\"documentId\":\"doc-demo-degree-001\"}" \
      "d.get('verified')==True"
  else
    warn "Skipping document tests (no auth token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "6. ADMIN API (Dev Mode)"
  # =========================================================================
  check_api "Admin doc-types" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/document-types" "" \
    "d.get('success') and len(d.get('documentTypes',[])) > 0"
  check_api "Admin workflows" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/workflows" "" \
    "d.get('success') and len(d.get('workflows',[])) > 0"
  check_api "Admin integrations" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/integrations" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_api "Admin settings" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/settings" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_api "Admin verification queue" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/verification-queue" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_http "System errors stats" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/system-errors/stats"
  # GDPR routes require authentication (security hardening)
  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    GDPR_RET=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$GATEWAY/originate/api/gdpr/retention" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$GDPR_RET" = "200" ]; then pass "GDPR retention (HTTP $GDPR_RET)"; else fail "GDPR retention — expected HTTP 200, got $GDPR_RET"; fi
    GDPR_DSR=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$GATEWAY/originate/api/gdpr/dsr/pending" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$GDPR_DSR" = "200" ]; then pass "GDPR DSR pending (HTTP $GDPR_DSR)"; else fail "GDPR DSR pending — expected HTTP 200, got $GDPR_DSR"; fi
  else
    warn "GDPR endpoints — skipped (no auth token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "7. INTEGRATION SERVICES"
  # =========================================================================
  TS_UUID=$(python3 -c "import uuid;print(str(uuid.uuid4()))" 2>/dev/null || echo "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000099")
  TS_HASH=$(python3 -c "import hashlib,time;print(hashlib.sha256(str(time.time()).encode()).hexdigest())" 2>/dev/null)
  check_api "Timestamping (create)" "POST" "http://localhost:6004/api/timestamps" \
    "{\"hash\":\"$TS_HASH\",\"timestampType\":\"rfc3161\",\"documentId\":\"$TS_UUID\"}" \
    "d.get('success')"

  check_api "M365 (init)" "POST" "http://localhost:6013/api/connections/init" \
    '{"tenantId":"smoke-test","connectionName":"Smoke","organizationId":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"}' \
    "d.get('success')"

  check_api "VC issue" "POST" "http://localhost:6014/api/credentials" \
    '{"documentId":"smoke-001","documentHash":"sha256:abcd","documentType":"DocumentCertification","documentTitle":"Smoke","issuerId":"i1","issuerName":"Smoke","subjectDid":"did:example:s","subjectName":"S"}' \
    "d.get('success') and d.get('credential',{}).get('@context')"

  # =========================================================================
  section "8. DATABASE PERSISTENCE"
  # =========================================================================
  # Verify the admin tables have data (proves DB init scripts ran)
  DB_TYPES=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6000/api/admin/document-types" 2>/dev/null)
  DB_COUNT=$(echo "$DB_TYPES" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('documentTypes',[])))" 2>/dev/null) || DB_COUNT=0
  if [ "$DB_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — document_type_configs ($DB_COUNT rows)"
  else
    fail "DB persistence — document_type_configs table empty or unreachable"
  fi

  DB_WORKFLOWS=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6000/api/admin/workflows" 2>/dev/null)
  DB_WF_COUNT=$(echo "$DB_WORKFLOWS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('workflows',[])))" 2>/dev/null) || DB_WF_COUNT=0
  if [ "$DB_WF_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — workflow_configs ($DB_WF_COUNT rows)"
  else
    fail "DB persistence — workflow_configs table empty or unreachable"
  fi

  # Verify auth tables (password reset, sessions)
  AUTH_HEALTH=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6003/health" 2>/dev/null)
  AUTH_DB=$(echo "$AUTH_HEALTH" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d.get('database','unknown'))" 2>/dev/null) || AUTH_DB="unknown"
  if [ "$AUTH_DB" = "connected" ] || [ "$AUTH_DB" = "healthy" ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — auth service database connected"
  else
    warn "DB persistence — auth service database: $AUTH_DB"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "9. MULTI-TENANCY & MCP SERVICES"
  # =========================================================================

  # Tokenisation service
  check_health "Tokenisation health" "http://localhost:6021/health"

  TOKENISE_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:6021/api/tokenise" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"tenantId":"smoke-test","data":{"name":"Smoke User","email":"smoke@test.io"},"fields":["name","email"],"key":"c29tZS10ZXN0LWtleS0zMi1ieXRlcy0xMjM0NQ=="}' 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$TOKENISE_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('success') or 'tokenised' in str(d) else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "Tokenisation — tokenise endpoint responds"
  else
    warn "Tokenisation — tokenise endpoint returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # Tenant provisioning
  check_health "Tenant Provisioning health" "http://localhost:6022/health"

  TENANT_LIST=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6022/api/tenants" 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$TENANT_LIST" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if isinstance(d,list) or d.get('success') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "Tenant Provisioning — list tenants responds"
  else
    warn "Tenant Provisioning — list tenants returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # MCP Server
  check_health "MCP Server health" "http://localhost:6023/health"

  MCP_HASH=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:6023/api/hash" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"content":"smoke-test-content"}' 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$MCP_HASH" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('hash') or d.get('success') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "MCP Server — hash endpoint works"
  else
    warn "MCP Server — hash endpoint returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # Platform API (requires admin token)
  ADMIN_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | \
    python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['accessToken'])" 2>/dev/null) || ADMIN_TOKEN=""

  if [ -n "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
    TENANT_API=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 \
      "$GATEWAY/api/platform/tenants" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 2>/dev/null) || TENANT_API="000"
    if [ "$TENANT_API" = "200" ]; then
      pass "Platform API — /api/platform/tenants (HTTP $TENANT_API)"
    else
      fail "Platform API — /api/platform/tenants (HTTP $TENANT_API)"
    fi
  else
    warn "Platform API — skipped (no admin token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "10. STRUCTURED LOGGING"
  # =========================================================================
  SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  # Verify services produce structured JSON logs (spot-check originate)
  LOG_LINE=$(docker compose -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.yml" logs originate 2>/dev/null | grep '"level"' | head -1) || LOG_LINE=""
  if [ -n "$LOG_LINE" ]; then
    pass "Structured logging — originate produces JSON logs"
  else
    warn "Structured logging — could not verify originate JSON logs"
  fi

  # Verify dev-default warnings appear
  JWT_WARN=$(docker compose -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.yml" logs originate 2>/dev/null | grep -c "development default") || JWT_WARN=0
  if [ "$JWT_WARN" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "Env validation — dev-default warnings present"
  else
    warn "Env validation — no dev-default warnings found"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "11. REDIS CONNECTIVITY"
  # =========================================================================
  REDIS_OK=$(docker exec secuura-redis redis-cli -a secuura_redis_dev ping 2>/dev/null) || REDIS_OK=""
  if [ "$REDIS_OK" = "PONG" ]; then
    pass "Redis — authenticated connection (PONG)"
  else
    fail "Redis — authentication failed or unreachable"
  fi
fi

# =========================================================================
section "RESULTS"
# =========================================================================
TOTAL=$((PASS + FAIL))
printf "\n  ${GREEN}Passed: $PASS${NC}  ${RED}Failed: $FAIL${NC}  ${YELLOW}Warnings: $WARN${NC}  Total: $TOTAL\n"

if [ $FAIL -gt 0 ]; then
  printf "\n  ${RED}FAILURES:${NC}\n"
  for f in "${FAILURES[@]}"; do
    printf "    ${RED}✗${NC} %s\n" "$f"
  done
  printf "\n"
  exit 1
else
  printf "\n  ${GREEN}All checks passed.${NC}\n\n"
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh - a FAILED per-image
# scan must never read as a CLEAN image (KS-1136 item 1, R-2)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: each image's scan was `raw="$(trivy image ... || echo '{}')"`, so a
# trivy that exited non-zero with no output became `{}`, and the jq that follows
# wrote `counts: {}` / `vulns: []` for that image - scanned and clean - with the
# job exiting 0. With partial output on one of two images, the artefact itself
# came out unparseable, still rc 0.
#
# docker and trivy are NEVER run here (no stack, no daemon): both are STUBS on
# a private PATH, in the shape of container_trivy_image_filter.test.sh. The
# trivy stub reads $root/fail.txt ("<image> empty|partial" per line) and fails
# that image's scan the way the gate measured; every other image gets `{}`.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/container_trivy_failed_scan_is_loud.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
JOB="$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh"
[ -f "$JOB" ] || { echo "FATAL: 04-container-trivy.sh not found at $JOB" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: jq is not on PATH - the subject cannot run, so nothing here can be graded" >&2; exit 2; }

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1136.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Build a fixture around the job under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = corpus text (what `docker images` prints)   $3 = fail list ("<image> empty|partial" lines)
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" corpus="$2" fails="${3:-}"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/Testing/jobs" "$root/bin" "$root/run"
  cp "$JOB" "$root/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh"
  printf '%s\n' "$corpus" > "$root/images.txt"
  printf '%s\n' "$fails" > "$root/fail.txt"
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'
    printf 'case "${1:-}" in\n'
    printf '  info) exit 0 ;;\n'
    printf '  images) cat "%s/images.txt" ;;\n' "$root"
    printf 'esac\nexit 0\n'
  } > "$root/bin/docker"
  sed "s#@ROOT@#$root#g" > "$root/bin/trivy" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
for last; do :; done
echo "$last" >> "@ROOT@/trivy_scanned.txt"
mode="$(awk -v i="$last" '$1 == i { print $2 }' "@ROOT@/fail.txt")"
case "$mode" in
  empty) exit 1 ;;
  partial) printf '{"Results":['; exit 1 ;;
esac
echo '{}'
STUB
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker" "$root/bin/trivy"
}

# Run the job the way the orchestrator / audit runner do. Prints rc.
run_job() {
  local root="$1"
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" SELF="$root/Testing" RUN_DIR="$root/run"
    cd "$SELF" && bash jobs/04-container-trivy.sh ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
art() { jq -r "$2" "$1/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null || echo unparseable; }

# CONTROL - every scan succeeds: rc 0, two images, no image carries an error.
build_fixture "$WORK/clean" 'dev-auth:latest
dev-api-gateway:latest'
rc="$(run_job "$WORK/clean")"
got="$rc $(art "$WORK/clean" '.images | length') $(art "$WORK/clean" '[.images[] | select(.error)] | length')"
if [ "$got" = "0 2 0" ]; then ok "CONTROL - two clean scans: rc 0, 2 images, 0 errors"; else bad "CONTROL - two clean scans: rc 0, 2 images, 0 errors" "want 0 2 0, got $got"; fi

# RED - the ONLY image's trivy exits 1 with NO output.
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" 'dev-auth:latest' 'dev-auth:latest empty'
rc="$(run_job "$WORK/empty")"
got="$rc $(art "$WORK/empty" '.images[0].error // "none"')"
if [ "$got" = "1 scan-failed" ]; then ok "🔴 a trivy that exits 1 with no output is recorded as scan-failed and the job exits 1"; else bad "🔴 a trivy that exits 1 with no output is recorded as scan-failed and the job exits 1" "want 1 scan-failed, got $got"; fi

# RED - one of two images fails with PARTIAL output; the other scans clean.
build_fixture "$WORK/partial" 'dev-auth:latest
dev-api-gateway:latest' 'dev-auth:latest partial'
rc="$(run_job "$WORK/partial")"
got="$rc $(art "$WORK/partial" '[.images[] | .error // "none"] | sort | join(",")')"
if [ "$got" = "1 none,scan-failed" ]; then ok "🔴 a partial-output failure on one of two images is recorded as scan-failed, the other stays clean, and the job exits 1"; else bad "🔴 a partial-output failure on one of two images is recorded as scan-failed, the other stays clean, and the job exits 1" "want 1 none,scan-failed, got $got"; fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
